nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a vector of length $n$, and consider the draw histories $d$, which assign to each position $i < n$ a number $d_i$ with $0 \le d_i < n - i$. For every outcome $o$ (a vector of length $n$ together with a cost pair), the probability that the Fisher–Yates output distribution of $x$ assigns to $o$ equals the sum, over all draw histories $d$ for which the Fisher–Yates computation on $x$ and $d$ yields exactly…
nodes.title: Probability of a Fisher–Yates outcome

nodes.summary: Let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a vector and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ chosen uniformly at random. Then the Fisher–Yates output distribution of $x$ equals the distribution of the outcome consisting of the vector $(x_{\sigma(0)}, \dots, x_{\sigma(n-1)})$ with cost pair $(n, n)$.
nodes.title: Fisher–Yates produces a uniformly random permutation

nodes.summary: For a vector $x$ of length $n$, this is the probability distribution on outcomes (a vector of length $n$ together with a cost pair in $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$) obtained by choosing a draw history $d$ uniformly at random among all assignments of a number $d_i$ with $0 \le d_i < n - i$ to each position $i < n$, and returning the result of the Fisher–Yates computation on $x$ and $d$.
nodes.title: Output distribution of the Fisher–Yates shuffle

nodes.summary: For the empty vector $x$ (of length $0$) and its empty draw history, the Fisher–Yates computation returns $x$ with cost pair $(0, 0)$: it retrieves no draws and performs no swaps.
nodes.title: Fisher–Yates on the empty vector

nodes.summary: For every vector $x$ of length $n$ and every draw history $d$, which assigns to each position $i < n$ a number $d_i$ with $0 \le d_i < n - i$, the list of entries of the vector returned by the Fisher–Yates computation on $x$ and $d$ is a permutation of the list of entries of $x$. In particular every value occurs equally often in both, even when values of $x$ repeat.
nodes.title: Fisher–Yates output is a rearrangement of its input

nodes.summary: Let $k \le n$ and let $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ be distinct elements of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$. Run the Fisher–Yates computation on the vector $(0, 1, \dots, n - 1)$ with every draw history $d$, which assigns to each position $i < n$ a number $d_i$ with $0 \le d_i < n - i$, and give each history weight $1/n!$. nodes.title: Prefix probabilities of the Fisher–Yates shuffle

nodes.summary: For every vector $x$ of length $1$ and every draw history $d$, the Fisher–Yates computation returns $x$ unchanged with cost pair $(1, 1)$: it still retrieves the single draw $d_0 = 0$ and performs the self-swap at position $0$.
nodes.title: Fisher–Yates on a one-element vector

nodes.summary: For every vector $x$ of length $n$ and every draw history $d$, which assigns to each position $i < n$ a number $d_i$ with $0 \le d_i < n - i$, the Fisher–Yates computation on $x$ and $d$ has cost pair $(n, n)$: it retrieves exactly $n$ draws and performs exactly $n$ swaps.
nodes.title: Cost of the Fisher–Yates shuffle

nodes.summary: Given a vector $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ and a draw history $d$, which assigns to each position $i < n$ a number $d_i$ with $0 \le d_i < n - i$, the Fisher–Yates computation processes the positions $i = 0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ in increasing order and at position $i$ swaps the entries at positions $i$ and $i + d_i$ of the current vector. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
